engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Strategy: Pawn Structure
chess.body: Your pawn structure dictates your plan. Doubled pawns (two pawns on same file) = weakness. Isolated pawn = can't be defended by a pawn, needs piece protection. Passed pawn = no enemy pawn can stop it = future queen. Backward pawn = can't advance, target for opponent. Know your pawn structure and play accordingly.

wisdom.title: The Compound Effect of Small Moments
wisdom.body: You don't build a relationship in big moments. You build it in 10,000 small ones. Morning hugs. Saying her name with warmth. Listening when she babbles even though you don't understand. These stack. In 15 years, she'll feel either deeply loved or quietly neglected. Both are built today.

book.author: Chris Voss
book.chapter: The Power of No and Calibrated Questions
book.lesson: Voss argues that 'no' is not the opposite of 'yes' in negotiation — it's the beginning. When someone says no, they feel safe. They feel in control. A fake yes (where they agree to get you off their back) is far worse than a genuine no. His technique: ask questions that invite 'no.' 'Is now a bad time to talk?' gets a more honest response than 'Is now a good time?' His other key tool: calibrated questions — open-ended questions starting with 'what' and 'how' that force the other person to problem-solve. 'How am I supposed to do that?' puts the problem back on them without being confrontational.
book.key_quote: 'No' means 'I'm not comfortable yet.' Your job is to find out what would make them comfortable.
book.action: In your next negotiation, replace 'Can you do X?' with 'How can we make X work?' Notice how differently people respond.
crux: Negotiation is not rational argument. It is emotional intelligence applied under pressure.
Tactical empathy: recognise and name the other side's perspective without agreeing to it.
Mirroring — repeat their last 1–3 words — keeps them talking and reveals information.
Labelling: 'It seems like…', 'It sounds like…'. Naming a negative defuses it.
Run an accusation audit — list their worst assumptions about you and say them first.
'No' is the start of the negotiation, not the end. It creates safety.
Aim for 'That's right', not 'You're right'. The second means they want you to stop.
Never split the difference. Compromise produces outcomes neither side wanted.
Deadlines are usually artificial and almost always work against whoever fears them.
The F-word: fairness. When they invoke it, they feel wronged. Address that, not the maths.
Bend their reality with anchoring, loss aversion, and non-round numbers.
Calibrated 'How' and 'What' questions transfer the problem without confrontation.
'How am I supposed to do that?' is the most useful sentence in the book.
Find the Black Swan — the unknown that reframes the whole deal. Three types of leverage: positive, negative, normative.
learnings: Listening is the tactic, not the courtesy.
Getting to 'no' early saves months of false progress.
Non-round numbers read as calculated; round numbers read as arbitrary.
Compromise is usually mutual loss wearing a diplomatic label.
examples: Voss talked down a Brooklyn bank robber using mirroring alone, with no tactical leverage available.
The Chase Manhattan hostage case: 'It seems like you don't want to go back to jail' opened a conversation that demands had closed.
A student negotiated a salary from $30k to $34k plus a defined promotion path by asking 'How am I supposed to accept that?'
adapt: Dubai salary talk: anchor with a non-round number — AED 32,400, not 30,000. Then ask how they can get there.
Accusation audit before the offer conversation: 'You're probably thinking I'm asking above the band for this level.'
Label the objection about not having UAE experience before they raise it.
Never split the difference on the SIP amount. Automate the number and remove the negotiation with yourself.

minimalism.title: Digital Minimalism First
minimalism.body: Physical clutter is visible and therefore self-limiting. Digital clutter is infinite. 40,000 unread emails and 200 apps cost more attention than a messy room ever did.
minimalism.action: Delete every app you have not opened in 30 days. No exceptions for 'might need'.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Introduce People Properly
etiquette.body: Do not just exchange names — give each person a reason to care. 'Sara, this is Ahmed, he rebuilt their close process in six weeks.' You have just made both look good.
etiquette.action: Make one introduction today with a reason attached.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: The Sabbath Principle
stillness.body: One day in seven with no optimisation, no side project, no market. Every durable tradition independently arrived at this. They were not being inefficient.
stillness.action: Block one screen-free half-day this week. Defend it.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Skin In The Game
model.body: Discount any forecast from someone who bears no cost for being wrong. Advice without exposure is entertainment, however credentialed the source.
model.action: For your next major input, ask what the adviser loses if they are wrong.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: Ends a discussion, confirms completion, or stops a child. One of the most-used words in the Gulf.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Sensitivity, Not Point Estimates
drill.body: A single number is a guess dressed up. Run it at -20%, base, and +20% and present the range. Nobody credible presents one number.
drill.action: Take one forecast. Build the three cases. Note which input moves it most.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Zone 2, Most Of The Time
health.body: Roughly 80% of cardio should be easy enough to hold a conversation. It builds mitochondrial density and fat oxidation. Most people train too hard to recover and too easy to adapt — the worst of both.
health.action: 45 minutes at a pace where you can speak in full sentences.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Gary Vaynerchuk
quote.quote: Patience is the key. We overestimate what we can do in a year and underestimate what we can do in a decade.

lesson.lesson: The function of leadership is to produce more leaders, not more followers.

case.title: Byju's: The EdTech Crash
case.story: Byju's raised $5.5B, was valued at $22B, and collapsed. No focus on profitability, weak governance, rapid expansion into unproven markets.
case.lesson: Capital is a drug. More money means more runway, but it also means you can delay facing hard truths. Profitability is always the destination.

fpna.title: Financial Storytelling
fpna.body: Data without narrative is noise. Frame every number: vs budget, vs prior year, vs industry.

cfo.title: FC Step 5: Treasury Basics
cfo.body: Cash flow forecasting, FX hedging policy, bank relationship management, working capital optimisation. The jump from FP&A to FC often requires you to pick up treasury. Start with 13-week cash flow models.

money_hack.title: NPS for Tax Saving
money_hack.body: ₹50K in NPS under 80CCD(1B) = ₹15K saved at 30% bracket. Plus retirement corpus.

dubai.title: Power BI is the tiebreaker
dubai.body: Between two CAs with identical FP&A experience, the one who can build the dashboard gets the offer. Not because the dashboard matters — because it proves you will not need an analyst.
dubai.targets: DAX, one real model, published. A certificate without an artefact proves nothing.
dubai.action: One dashboard on your own trading ledger. It is real data and it is defensible.

desk.productivity: Done > perfect. Ship at 80%, iterate on real feedback.

father.title: Stop at eye contact
father.do: When she catches your eye across the room, stop and respond — smile, wave, say her name.
father.why: Social referencing is beginning: she checks your face to decide how to feel about things. Responding consistently makes you a reliable reference point.

father.title: Let her lead the play
father.do: Follow what she reaches for instead of redirecting to the toy you chose. Sit on the floor at her level for 15 minutes.
father.why: Serve-and-return interaction builds the circuitry for attention and self-regulation. Following her focus teaches that her signals produce a response — the root of secure attachment.

life_wisdom.teaching: A periodic practice of reviewing one's conduct, acknowledging where one fell short, and resolving to correct it. Structurally, an audit.
life_wisdom.apply: You already run a monthly close on the business. Run a fifteen-minute one on yourself: what did I get wrong, what am I changing, what is the date.

life_wisdom.teaching: In the traditional sequence of practices, generosity comes before ethics and meditation — as the foundation rather than the reward.
life_wisdom.apply: Give something away before you feel you have surplus. Time or attention counts; the point is that it precedes abundance rather than following it.

speaking.title: Handle the interruption
speaking.drill: Rehearse: 'Let me finish this point, then I will take that.' Say it out loud five times until it sounds calm rather than defensive.
speaking.why: Being talked over in a board meeting is a delivery problem, not a rank problem.

interview_tech.q: How do you account for customer loyalty points under IFRS 15?
interview_tech.a: Points are a separate performance obligation. You allocate part of the original transaction price to the points based on their standalone selling price, adjusted for expected breakage, and defer that portion as contract liability. Revenue is recognised when points are redeemed or expire. Practically: the deferral reduces reported revenue today, and the breakage estimate is a judgement auditors probe every year. Retailers who ignore this overstate current-period revenue and get a restatement.

interview_tech.q: A category has 40% gross margin but negative contribution. How?
interview_tech.a: Gross margin ignores everything below the line. That category may carry disproportionate space, handling cost, markdown, shrink or return rate. Bulky low-value goods are the classic case — good percentage margin, terrible margin per square metre per week. Move to a contribution view: gross profit less directly attributable space, labour, logistics and markdown. Assortment decisions made on gross margin percentage alone are how retailers end up with profitable-looking categories that lose money.

interview_soft.q: How do you decide what to delegate?
interview_soft.a: Give a rule. Something like: delegate anything where the cost of a mistake is recoverable and the learning value is high; keep anything where your specific judgement is the reason the answer is right, and anything you would have to redo. The failure mode interviewers probe is the controller who keeps the technical work because it is comfortable and delegates only the admin — which caps the team's growth and yours.

interview_soft.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your CEO.
interview_soft.a: They are testing whether you have spine and judgement, not whether you win. Use STAR and pick a disagreement where you were partly wrong — it reads as honest. Cover: what the disagreement was, what evidence you brought, how you escalated it appropriately, what the decision was, and crucially what you did after the decision went against you. The signal they want: you argue hard privately and commit fully publicly.
